title: PaySwap3 governance model
description: Machine-readable summary of the governance contracts under spec/governance/. The markdown contracts are authoritative for detail; this file mirrors them for tooling and must be updated in lockstep with them by the post-merge reconciliation duties.

authority_precedence.authoritative_for: financial semantics: authority, accounting, execution, clearing, netting, settlement, finality
nothing; projections never authorize work and lose against Git facts

same_rank_rule: Same-rank authorities of different layers govern only their own layer; cross-layer conflicts are reconciliation findings, not precedence wins.

Architect.scope: Architecture, review, and merge authority for the repository.
permissions: own and maintain the frozen protocol architecture under spec/architecture/v0.1/
run the Architecture Change Request process for any protocol semantic change
review and approve or reject pull requests at the review gates
merge verified pull requests (sole merge authority)
resolve ARCHITECTURE_BLOCKER escalations and reclassify standing red flags
audit layer state files and derived projections against Git facts
convene three-layer reconciliation before any declaration of system completion
prohibitions: delegate merge authority to the Tech Lead or to workers
accept green tests without contract review
alter frozen protocol semantics outside the Architecture Change Request process
declare system completion before three-layer reconciliation and operational evidence

Tech Lead.scope: Planning, eligibility computation, dispatch, integration, and evidence enforcement.
permissions: plan work and decompose it into bounded work items
dispatch workers with complete, schema-valid execution contexts
integrate verified changes and prepare them for Architect review
enforce evidence requirements and dogfooding standards
drive product and deployment completion work
escalate architecture questions to the Architect
prohibitions: merge pull requests (merge authority rests with the Architect alone)
expand a worker's assigned scope beyond its contract
treat chat memory as architecture or project state
let sibling workers consume unmerged sibling code
weaken assurance requirements to gain parallelism

Worker.scope: Bounded implementation of exactly one assigned work item under one explicit contract.
permissions: create and work on the single branch for the assigned work item
create and modify only the owned surfaces listed in the execution context
fix WITHIN_SCOPE drift findings inside the assigned work item
report blockers and escalate per the escalation rule
produce the required proofs and dogfooding evidence
prohibitions: merge the worker's own pull request
touch forbidden surfaces or expand assigned scope
invent product scope, protocol semantics, or a parallel governance model
enter secrets into git, work-item text, pull request descriptions, or worker reports
proceed on any drift classification other than WITHIN_SCOPE

merge_rule.statement: A pull request is merged only by the Architect, only after every review gate passes; the worker who authored the change never merges it.

definitions.WITHIN_SCOPE: Defect fully inside the assigned work item: owned surfaces, contract scope, no authority or semantic implications. The only classification that may be fixed inside the work item.
definitions.OUT_OF_SCOPE: Real issue outside the work item's owned surfaces or purpose. Do not fix locally; record and escalate.
definitions.CONTRACT_BLOCKER: The work order contract is ambiguous, internally inconsistent, or impossible as given. Stop and escalate to the Tech Lead.
definitions.ARCHITECTURE_BLOCKER: Contradiction with frozen architecture, the authority model, or repository facts. Stop and escalate via the Tech Lead to the Architect.
definitions.ENVIRONMENT_BLOCKER: Tooling, access, or environment failure the worker must not resolve unilaterally. Stop and escalate with diagnostics.

drift_control.standing_rule: Only WITHIN_SCOPE findings may be fixed inside the assigned work item; every other classification is stop-and-escalate.

escalation_rule.statement: Stop-and-escalate on any blocker classification other than WITHIN_SCOPE.
escalation_rule.within_scope: may be fixed inside the assigned work item and reported
escalation_rule.all_other_classifications: stop work immediately, preserve evidence, escalate; never solve locally

routing.OUT_OF_SCOPE: Tech Lead (records a new work item or reassigns)

secrets_policy.statement: Secrets never enter git history, work-item text, pull request descriptions, or worker reports.
secrets_policy.on_discovery: Report the location only, never the value; classify per spec/governance/drift-control.md and stop if handling the secret would be required.

sibling_isolation.statement: Sibling workers never consume unmerged sibling code; a worker builds only on merged main at the exact base SHA recorded in the execution context.
sibling_isolation.base_movement: When main moves because a sibling merges, the Tech Lead issues a sibling-wave update with the new base SHA; dependent re-dispatch follows the merge, not the branch.

validation.scope: authority path existence (with explicit sibling-wave accounting), governance model classification enum, execution-context schema parse and example validation, GOV-001 surface self-check
